claims.text: Conventional steel components are used in high-temperature liquid-aluminum environments during hot-dip aluminum plating.
Conventional steel components should be replaced with nickel-based superalloy components.
Nickel-based superalloys are more corrosion resistant than conventional steels in high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Nickel-based superalloys have superior oxidation resistance because of their alloying elements and microstructure.
Nickel-based superalloys have superior corrosion resistance because of their alloying elements and microstructure.
The alloying elements and microstructure of nickel-based superalloys enable them to withstand attack by liquid aluminum.
Nickel-based superalloy components will experience less corrosion than conventional steel components under hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
Nickel-based superalloy components will experience less wear than conventional steel components under hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
Nickel-based superalloy components will have a service life at least 50% longer than conventional steel components.
The proposed benefit is limited to components directly contacting high-temperature liquid aluminum during plating.
The service-life improvement may vary with nickel-based superalloy composition and operating conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 50% service-life extension, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant reduction in corrosion and wear. A small statistically significant improvement could therefore pass the experiment while failing the stated 50% outcome.
